title: The guard refuses `git checkout -B` or `switch -C` of a branch another worktree holds
why: Lane fix-check-after-notes-commit saw it twice on Nov 7 (record commit 9b2a11b9e, builder commit 391d4deea). Three worktrees held one branch through `git checkout -B <branch>`. A commit from one carried a stale index and undid another worktree's pushed work. The harm is a silent undo of pushed code.
note: Remedy line: `git checkout --detach origin/<branch>`, then `git push origin HEAD:<branch>`. Built by guard two-worktrees-one-branch, in lane session_013NEJKyzA8bkZSm147VHnke, which is in review round 2 and has reproduced this incident. That lane also covers `switch -C` (coordinator, 15:53 CST). Related steps: checkout-b-current-branch, agent-push-moves-held-branch and worktree-unique-branch. Done check: a red test on -B of a branch that another worktree holds. Sighting 10:05 CST Nov 8 (lane pr-review-range-check): two agent briefs both ran `checkout -B review-range-check` in separate worktrees; the test-author's push moved the branch under the builder's tree and left it stale. This is the step's own case. Sighting (lane lane-lint-before-push, #2077, 11:25 CST Nov 8), twice today: a builder resumed into the session's own worktree after a worker restart ran `git checkout -B <branch>` and committed on the branch that worktree held, so the ref moved and the files stayed at the old commit. Nothing was lost; a later `git commit -a` there would silently revert the agent's work. The lane asks the guard to cover `branch -f` and `update-ref` of a branch another worktree holds too. Workaround in its briefs: push `HEAD:<branch>` from an agent-own branch. Lane override-plain-ask 11:27 CST Nov 8: the guard never landed; #1583 is an open draft in conflict with main, as are #1463 and #1513 (stacked on #1463); the lane merges main into #1463 and #1583 and hands them back to the batch runner. `git branch -f` of a held branch is refused by git itself (measured 2026-11-07); `update-ref` is unproven, filed as outbox note update-ref-held-branch. Open question to lane lane-lint-before-push: was the shell's cwd another checkout when `checkout -B` left the files stale? If so #1583 refuses it. Sighting (lane notes-count-reader, session_013NEJKzEeXJNdTNedKPwtGc, 11:51 CST Nov 8): two of its agents' worktrees held the same local branch; one agent's commit moved the other's HEAD and left a stale index, costing two respawns. Lane proposes asking on `git worktree add`, `switch` or `checkout` to a local branch another worktree holds, and briefs that name a per-agent branch. Lane to confirm scope. Incident (coordinator 13:24 CST Nov 8): lane input-needed-reads-page-status (session_013NEJL3UmACWzQ3FibMH7ad) had two agent worktrees check out the same branch name; each later held a stale staged copy that blocked a commit. #1583 covers it. Coordinator 15:55 CST Nov 8: carried by #1583 in lane override-plain-ask (session_013NEJKyzA8bkZSm147VHnke), step two-worktrees-one-branch; step checkout-b-current-branch folds in here.
